title: The context window: a chatbot's working memory
summary: The context window is everything a model can reference while replying: the messages, documents and the reply itself. Too long and the request is rejected, or old turns drop out.

beats.say: A chatbot's working memory is a window of fixed size.
The context window is everything the model can reference while replying.
That includes the messages, the documents, and the reply itself.

data.total: all of it counts toward the window

beats.say: OpenAI defines it as the maximum tokens in a single request.
OpenAI's count includes input, output, and reasoning tokens.
If the input alone is too large, the API returns an error.
beats.cap: Too long: the request is rejected

beats.say: Chat apps can manage a full window by dropping the oldest turns first.
Forgetting here means old text is no longer in the window.
Windows are measured in tokens, so how much fits depends on the text.
Inside the window, text is used. Outside it, it is not.

claims.note: Anthropic docs: if the input alone is too large, the API returns a 400 invalid_request_error ('prompt is too long')

facts.claim: Anthropic's documentation defines the context window as all the text a language model can reference when generating a response, including the response itself, and calls it the model's working memory
facts.note: Claude Platform docs, Context windows: definition and 'working memory'

facts.claim: Everything in the request counts toward the window: the system prompt, every message including tool results and documents, and the output counts too
facts.note: Claude Platform docs: what counts toward the context window

facts.claim: If the input alone is too large the API returns a 400 invalid_request_error ('prompt is too long'), and chat interfaces can manage the window on a rolling first-in, first-out basis
facts.note: Claude Platform docs: when the window is full

facts.claim: OpenAI defines the context window as the maximum number of tokens in a single request, including input, output and reasoning tokens
facts.note: OpenAI API docs, Conversation state: 'the maximum number of tokens that can be used in a single request'; includes input, output, and reasoning tokens
